title: Structured waivers
description: waivers/*.yaml. A waiver is not an ignored warning: it is a recorded engineering decision with a reason, evidence, an approver and a review condition. Nothing in this pipeline is suppressed silently, ERC warnings included.

target.description: What is being waived. Matched on stable fields so a waiver cannot accidentally widen to unrelated findings.

erc_code.description: KiCad ERC violation type, for ERC waivers.

reason.description: The engineering justification. 'Not important' is not a reason.

supporting_refs.description: Non-document evidence, e.g. 'schematic/J4' for a rail fed through a connector.

scope.description: How far this waiver reaches. Narrow scope is the default; a project-wide waiver needs a strong reason.

safety_related.description: True forces human approval regardless of the gate's own approval setting.

approver.description: Human who accepted the risk. Must be on the project reviewer roster. Never written by an agent.

expires.description: Waivers for time-decaying facts (supplier stock, provisional datasheets) must expire.

review_condition.description: What would invalidate this waiver, e.g. 'revisit if the 3V3 load exceeds 300 mA'.

then.description: Safety waivers must name what would trigger re-review; an open-ended safety waiver is not acceptable.
